forum

/FOR-uhm/ - the stress falls on FOR · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Forum means a place or medium for open discussion.

Once a month the co-op turns its loading dock into a forum where farmers and chefs argue prices, trade rumors, and settle next season's plantings.

Example

For ninety years the almanac's letters page has been the growers' forum: a question about blight posted in March gathers a dozen answers by June, and feuds over pruning methods have run, politely, for decades.

A forum is defined by exchange: many voices, questions meeting answers, disagreement out in the open. A lecture has one speaker and a silent room; a bulletin board only posts notices. Call something a forum when discussion is the point.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

symposium: A symposium is a formal conference where invited experts present to one another — the guest list is credentials. A forum is open to all comers: anyone may raise a question or offer an answer. If speaking rights come with an invitation, it is a symposium, not a forum.

assembly: An assembly is any large gathering convened for an occasion — it may sit silent while one voice speaks. A forum exists specifically for open exchange: the discussion, not the crowd, is the point. Every forum runs on questions and answers; only some gatherings let anyone talk back.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

monologue: one voice holding forth, with no exchange at all

soapbox: a perch for broadcasting opinions, not trading them

Where it sits · how many voices are let in — huddle → meeting → forum

huddle vs. forum: A huddle is a few insiders talking privately; it stops far short of a forum's open doors.

meeting vs. forum: A meeting goes further than a huddle — an agenda, a table, invited voices — but a forum outdoes both by throwing the discussion open to whoever walks in.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — forum

Root — forum: the public square of a Roman town (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Forum is a straight borrowing: in a Roman town, the forum was the open square where markets, trials and speeches all happened. English kept the idea and loosened the geography — a letters page, a website or a parish hall can now be a forum, so long as the public can speak there. There is nothing to peel off; the word arrived in one piece.

Use the root in a new word: forensic

Use the root in a new word: forensic: The forensic accountant traced the missing money the way courtroom experts trace fingerprints.

Strength Check

Word Choice

neutral / civic

Forum stresses openness: a place or channel where many voices can question and answer. A symposium belongs to experts, a panel to its panelists, an assembly to whoever convened it. If the defining feature is that anyone may speak, forum is the word.
